This page holds the exercise of the course, Tasks 1 to 5, on a copy of R that runs inside the browser, with the data already in place and the same helper functions as the downloadable workspace. It is the page the facilitator drives on the shared screen, a place to try the analysis and the data before you have installed anything, and the fallback for a machine that will not cooperate on the day. The course's own work is done in the workspace from the [Setup](../setup.qmd) page; nothing you do here is lost by that, since the numbers are the same.

::: {.callout-important icon="false"}
## While the R engine loads

The R engine downloads into your browser the first time you open this page (10–30 seconds on a slow connection) – read Task 1 while it warms up. You will see the first code cell switch from a loading spinner to a "Run Code" button when it is ready.

Keep this tab open. Your work lives in this page until you refresh – there is nothing to install, nothing to save to disk, and no account needed.
:::

```{webr}
#| include: false
#| autorun: true
# Lab machinery – the fourteen-decision specification menu, its validation,
# and the helper functions that the exercise flow uses. Participants interact
# with try_spec(), my_experiments(), submit_exploration(), prereg(),
# build_model(), run_spec() and report_result(). Every result they print is
# read from the pre-computed maximal grid, which the site serves as one small
# file per estimand cell: the six Level 1 choices (the question) name the file,
# and the eight Level 2 and 3 choices (the measurement and the arithmetic) pick
# the row inside it. No model is fitted in the browser, so none of the
# estimation packages is downloaded. Shards are fetched on demand from the
# published site – an absolute address, because a relative one would resolve
# against the WebAssembly worker rather than this page.
.site <- "https://codemoreh.github.io/applied-replication"
.neg_framings <- c("mcomm", "mlib", "mneg")
.outcomes     <- c("mcosmo", "mutil", "mcomm", "mlib", "mpos", "mneg")

# The menu, grouped as the course groups it. Level 1 changes the question,
# Level 2 the measurement, Level 3 the estimation. The scoring rule is a
# Level 1 decision: a share of a respondent's own mentions and a count of the
# set's items are different quantities, and the per-item rate is the count
# divided by the number of items in the set.
.menu <- list(
  # Level 1 – Estimands
  my_outcome      = .outcomes,
  my_predictor    = c("unemp", "growth"),
  my_copredictor  = c("none", "other"),
  my_estimator    = c("fe_twoway", "fe_country", "re", "pooled_cl"),
  my_sample       = c("all", "y2004_2008", "y2009_2013", "no_bailout", "no_GR_ES"),
  my_weights      = c("none", "n_cell", "n_eff", "pop"),
  my_construction = c("share", "count", "rate"),
  # Level 2 – Measurement
  my_noop         = c("zero", "drop", "split", "mi_mice", "mi_amelia"),
  my_item_set     = c("all", "un"),
  my_cell_weight  = c("unweighted", "design"),
  my_measure      = c("wb_nat", "es_1574_act", "es_2064_pop", "es_2564_lfs", "es_1574_tips",
                      "wb_growth", "es_growth"),
  # Level 3 – Estimation
  my_pred_form    = c("raw", "log"),
  my_family       = c("gaussian", "beta"),
  my_se           = c("conventional", "clustered")
)
.measures_for <- list(unemp  = c("wb_nat", "es_1574_act", "es_2064_pop", "es_2564_lfs", "es_1574_tips"),
                      growth = c("wb_growth", "es_growth"))

.est_lab <- function(e) c(
  fe_twoway  = "two-way fixed effects (country + year)",
  fe_country = "country fixed effects",
  re         = "random effects",
  pooled_cl  = "pooled OLS")[[e]]

# The term for the claim-carrying predictor as it appears in a formula:
# log(unemp) when the log form is chosen, else the bare variable name.
.main_term <- function(ch) {
  if (ch$my_predictor == "unemp" && ch$my_pred_form == "log") "log(unemp)"
  else ch$my_predictor
}
.copred_term <- function(ch) if (ch$my_predictor == "unemp") "growth" else "unemp"

# the measurement settings at which the beta family was pre-computed
.canonical_measurement <- function(ch)
  ch$my_construction %in% c("share", "rate") && ch$my_noop == "zero" && ch$my_item_set == "all" &&
  ch$my_cell_weight == "unweighted" && ch$my_measure %in% c("wb_nat", "wb_growth")

# --- validation ------------------------------------------------------------
# Two entry points into the same rules. .validate() takes a named list, which
# is how the exploratory try_spec() supplies its arguments; .check_choices()
# reads the fourteen my_* choices and claim_align out of the session, which is
# how the declared flow reads the preregistration cell.
.validate <- function(ch, as_args = FALSE) {
  # the earlier menu named the co-predictor by its variable and called the
  # respondent-count weight n_cy; both spellings still work
  if (identical(ch$my_copredictor, .copred_term(ch))) ch$my_copredictor <- "other"
  if (identical(ch$my_weights, "n_cy")) ch$my_weights <- "n_cell"
  for (k in names(.menu)) {
    v <- ch[[k]]
    shown <- if (as_args) sub("^my_", "", k) else k
    if (is.null(v) || !is.character(v) || length(v) != 1 || !v %in% .menu[[k]])
      stop(sprintf("%s = \"%s\" is not on the menu. Options: %s.",
                   shown, paste(v, collapse = ","),
                   paste(.menu[[k]], collapse = " | ")), call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (ch$my_estimator == "re" && ch$my_weights != "none")
    stop("The random-effects estimator is never fitted with weights. Use weights = \"none\" or pick another estimator.",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (ch$my_predictor == "growth" && ch$my_pred_form == "log")
    stop("GDP growth enters raw only – it takes negative values, so the log is undefined. Use pred_form = \"raw\".",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (!ch$my_measure %in% .measures_for[[ch$my_predictor]])
    stop(sprintf("measure = \"%s\" is a series for %s; with predictor = \"%s\" choose one of: %s.",
                 ch$my_measure, setdiff(names(.measures_for), ch$my_predictor), ch$my_predictor,
                 paste(.measures_for[[ch$my_predictor]], collapse = " | ")), call. = FALSE)
  if (ch$my_family == "beta" && !.canonical_measurement(ch))
    stop("The beta family is pre-computed at the canonical measurement settings only: construction = \"share\" or \"rate\" (a count is not a proportion), noop = \"zero\", item_set = \"all\", cell_weight = \"unweighted\", measure = the World Bank series.",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (ch$my_family == "beta" && ch$my_estimator == "re" && ch$my_se == "clustered")
    stop("Clustered errors are not available for the beta random-effects fit. Use se = \"conventional\" with that pairing.",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (ch$my_noop %in% c("mi_mice", "mi_amelia") &&
      !(ch$my_construction == "share" && ch$my_item_set == "all" &&
        ch$my_cell_weight == "unweighted" && ch$my_measure == "wb_nat" &&
        ch$my_predictor == "unemp" && ch$my_pred_form == "raw" && ch$my_family == "gaussian"))
    stop("The imputed no-opinion options were pre-computed for the unemployment arm at the canonical measurement and estimation settings only (share, all items, unweighted cells, World Bank series, raw form, gaussian).",
         call. = FALSE)
  ch
}

.check_choices <- function() {
  need <- names(.menu)
  missing <- need[!vapply(need, exists, logical(1))]
  if (length(missing) > 0)
    stop("Not declared yet: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
         ". Fill in every choice in the preregistration cell and run it first.",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (!exists("claim_align"))
    stop("Also declare claim_align <- TRUE (the course convention) in the preregistration cell.",
         call. = FALSE)
  ch <- lapply(need, function(k) get(k))
  names(ch) <- need
  .validate(ch)
}

# --- the pre-computed universe ---------------------------------------------
# One file per estimand cell, named by the six Level 1 choices. A shard is
# fetched the first time a cell is asked for and kept for the session; the
# manifest (mounted with the page) says how many rows a complete shard has.
.shards <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
.cell_id <- function(ch)
  paste(ch$my_outcome, ch$my_predictor, ch$my_copredictor, ch$my_estimator,
        ch$my_sample, ch$my_weights, sep = "__")

.shard <- function(ch) {
  id <- .cell_id(ch)
  if (!is.null(.shards[[id]])) return(.shards[[id]])
  dir.create("data/grid", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
  f <- file.path("data/grid", paste0(id, ".csv.gz"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) {
    ok <- tryCatch({
      utils::download.file(paste0(.site, "/data/grid/", id, ".csv.gz"), f, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
      TRUE
    }, error = function(e) FALSE, warning = function(w) FALSE)
    if (!ok || !file.exists(f))
      stop(sprintf("Could not fetch the results for this question (cell %s). Check the connection and rerun; if it keeps failing, tell the facilitator the cell name and the numbers can be read off the grid by hand.", id),
           call. = FALSE)
  }
  d <- utils::read.csv(gzfile(f), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  if (file.exists("data/grid/manifest.csv")) {
    man <- utils::read.csv("data/grid/manifest.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    want <- man$rows[man$cell == id]
    if (length(want) == 1 && nrow(d) != want)
      stop(sprintf("The fetched file for cell %s is incomplete (%d of %d rows) – rerun the cell.", id, nrow(d), want),
           call. = FALSE)
  }
  .shards[[id]] <- d
  d
}

.lookup <- function(ch) {
  d <- .shard(ch)
  hit <- d[d$construction == ch$my_construction & d$item_set == ch$my_item_set &
           d$noop == ch$my_noop & d$cell_weight == ch$my_cell_weight &
           d$measure == ch$my_measure & d$pred_form == ch$my_pred_form &
           d$family == ch$my_family & d$se == ch$my_se, ]
  if (nrow(hit) != 1)
    stop(sprintf("That specification is not in the pre-computed universe (%d matching rows) – this should not happen for a menu-valid choice; tell the facilitator.", nrow(hit)),
         call. = FALSE)
  if (is.na(hit$estimate) || is.na(hit$statistic))
    stop("That specification did not fit when the grid was computed (the beta family under population weights is the known case). Choose another weight or the gaussian family.",
         call. = FALSE)
  hit
}

# The claim-alignment factor: negative framings are reverse-coded (1 - y), and
# the claim-expected sign for growth is positive, so each flips the reported
# sign. Reverse-coding is exact for both families (for beta,
# logit(1 - mu) = -logit(mu)), so the factor gives the claim-aligned numbers
# without a refit. The grid's own r_ca column is that aligned correlation.
.flip <- function(ch)
  (if (ch$my_outcome %in% .neg_framings) -1 else 1) *
  (if (ch$my_predictor == "growth") -1 else 1)

# The one-line spec label that the class chart reads: the six Level 1 choices,
# then the measurement and estimation choices in brackets.
.spec_line <- function(ch) {
  neg <- ch$my_outcome %in% .neg_framings
  paste0(ch$my_outcome, if (neg) "_ca" else "", " ~ ", ch$my_predictor, "(", ch$my_pred_form, ")",
         if (ch$my_copredictor == "other") paste0(" + ", .copred_term(ch)) else "",
         " | ", ch$my_estimator, " | ", ch$my_sample, " | w:", ch$my_weights,
         " [", ch$my_construction, ", ", ch$my_noop, ", items:", ch$my_item_set, ", cells:",
         ch$my_cell_weight, ", ", ch$my_measure, " | ", ch$my_family, ", se:", ch$my_se, "]")
}

# Where a result sits in the canonical 840: the share of that universe that
# supports the claim more strongly (a more negative aligned r).
.placement <- function(r_ca) {
  if (!file.exists("data/grid/canonical_rca.csv")) return(NA_real_)
  canon <- utils::read.csv("data/grid/canonical_rca.csv")
  mean(canon$r_ca < r_ca, na.rm = TRUE)
}

.print_fit <- function(ch, hit, lead) {
  stat_lab <- if (ch$my_family == "beta") "z" else "t"
  fl <- .flip(ch)
  cat(lead, "\n")
  cat("  ", .spec_line(ch), "\n", sep = "")
  cat(sprintf("  b = %.5f   se = %.5f   %s = %.3f on %d df   p %s\n",
              fl * hit$estimate, hit$std_error, stat_lab, fl * hit$statistic, round(hit$df),
              if (hit$p < 0.001) "< 0.001" else sprintf("= %.3f", hit$p)))
  cat(sprintf("  claim-aligned partial r = %.3f   (below zero supports the claim)\n", hit$r_ca))
  pl <- .placement(hit$r_ca)
  if (!is.na(pl))
    cat(sprintf("  placement: %.0f%% of the canonical 840 specifications support the claim more strongly than this one\n",
                100 * pl))
  if (startsWith(ch$my_noop, "mi_"))
    cat(sprintf("  (pooled over 10 imputations by Rubin's rules; fraction of missing information %.3f)\n", hit$fmi))
}

# --- Task 4: the exploratory helpers ---------------------------------------
.tried <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
.tried$log <- NULL
.tried$last <- NULL

try_spec <- function(outcome = "mcosmo", predictor = "unemp", copredictor = "none",
                     estimator = "fe_twoway", sample = "all", weights = "none",
                     construction = "share", noop = "zero", item_set = "all",
                     cell_weight = "unweighted", measure = NULL,
                     pred_form = "raw", family = "gaussian", se = "conventional") {
  if (is.null(measure)) measure <- if (predictor == "unemp") "wb_nat" else "wb_growth"
  ch <- .validate(list(my_outcome = outcome, my_predictor = predictor, my_copredictor = copredictor,
                       my_estimator = estimator, my_sample = sample, my_weights = weights,
                       my_construction = construction, my_noop = noop, my_item_set = item_set,
                       my_cell_weight = cell_weight, my_measure = measure,
                       my_pred_form = pred_form, my_family = family, my_se = se), as_args = TRUE)
  hit <- .lookup(ch)
  .print_fit(ch, hit, "")
  fl  <- .flip(ch)
  row <- as.data.frame(setNames(as.list(unlist(ch)), sub("^my_", "", names(ch))),
                       stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  row$b <- fl * hit$estimate; row$t <- fl * hit$statistic
  row$r_aligned <- hit$r_ca; row$sig <- hit$p < 0.05
  .tried$log  <- rbind(.tried$log, row)
  .tried$last <- list(ch = ch, hit = hit)
  invisible(row)
}

# The running log of everything try_spec() has looked up. Only the axes that
# varied are shown; the constant ones are the baseline.
my_experiments <- function() {
  if (is.null(.tried$log)) {
    cat("Nothing tried yet – call try_spec() at least once.\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  d <- .tried$log
  axes <- sub("^my_", "", names(.menu))
  varied <- axes[vapply(d[axes], function(x) length(unique(x)) > 1, logical(1))]
  show <- d[, c(varied, "b", "t", "r_aligned", "sig"), drop = FALSE]
  show$b <- signif(show$b, 3); show$t <- round(show$t, 2)
  show$r_aligned <- round(show$r_aligned, 3)
  cat("Specifications you have tried (", nrow(d), "):\n\n", sep = "")
  print(show, row.names = FALSE)
  cat("\nSpread of claim-aligned r: ",
      sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", min(d$r_aligned), max(d$r_aligned)),
      "  |  significant: ", sum(d$sig), " of ", nrow(d), "\n", sep = "")
  invisible(show)
}

submit_exploration <- function() {
  if (is.null(.tried$last))
    stop("Nothing to submit – call try_spec() first, ending with the specification you want on the chart.",
         call. = FALSE)
  .submit(.tried$last$ch, .tried$last$hit, "explore",
          "Your exploratory submission (claim-aligned, the last specification you tried):")
}

# --- Task 5: the declared helpers ------------------------------------------

prereg <- function() {
  ch  <- .check_choices()
  neg <- ch$my_outcome %in% .neg_framings
  cat("DECLARED – one specification, recorded before seeing its result:\n\n")
  cat("  The question (Level 1)\n")
  cat("    outcome    :", ch$my_outcome,
      if (neg) "(negative framing – reverse-coded automatically)" else "", "\n")
  cat("    predictor  :", ch$my_predictor,
      if (ch$my_predictor == "growth") "(claim-expected sign flipped automatically)" else "", "\n")
  cat("    adjusted   :", if (ch$my_copredictor == "other") .copred_term(ch) else "nothing", "\n")
  cat("    estimator  :", .est_lab(ch$my_estimator), "\n")
  cat("    sample     :", ch$my_sample, "   whose average:", ch$my_weights, "\n")
  cat("    scored as  :", ch$my_construction, "\n")
  cat("  The measurement (Level 2)\n")
  cat("    no-opinion rule:", ch$my_noop, "  items:", ch$my_item_set, "\n")
  cat("    cells:", ch$my_cell_weight, "  series:", ch$my_measure, "\n")
  cat("  The estimation (Level 3)\n")
  cat("    form:", ch$my_pred_form, "  family:", ch$my_family, "  errors:", ch$my_se, "\n")
  cat("  claim_align:", isTRUE(claim_align), "\n\n")
  cat("These choices are now fixed for the rest of the session – the later\n")
  cat("cells read them from here. Copy this cell into your notes: it is your\n")
  cat("preregistration record, made before you see the result.\n")
  invisible(ch)
}

build_model <- function(formula, estimator) {
  ch <- .check_choices()
  if (missing(formula) || !inherits(formula, "formula"))
    stop("The first argument must be a formula: outcome ~ predictor terms, unquoted.",
         call. = FALSE)
  lhs <- all.vars(formula[[2]])
  if (!identical(lhs, ch$my_outcome))
    stop(sprintf("The outcome in your formula is '%s' but you preregistered '%s'. The preregistration is binding – fix the formula, not the prereg.",
                 deparse(formula[[2]]), ch$my_outcome), call. = FALSE)
  want <- c(.main_term(ch), if (ch$my_copredictor == "other") .copred_term(ch))
  got  <- attr(terms(formula), "term.labels")
  if (!setequal(got, want))
    stop(sprintf("Right-hand side mismatch: you wrote { %s } but your preregistration implies { %s }.%s",
                 paste(got, collapse = ", "), paste(want, collapse = ", "),
                 if (.main_term(ch) == "log(unemp)" && !"log(unemp)" %in% got)
                   " You preregistered the log form – write log(unemp) in the formula." else ""),
         call. = FALSE)
  if (missing(estimator) || !identical(estimator, ch$my_estimator))
    stop(sprintf("estimator = \"%s\" does not match your preregistered \"%s\".",
                 if (missing(estimator)) "" else estimator, ch$my_estimator), call. = FALSE)
  cat("Model accepted – it matches your preregistration exactly:\n")
  cat("  ", deparse(formula), ", estimated by ", .est_lab(estimator), "\n", sep = "")
  cat("  Run it with run_spec(my_model).\n")
  structure(list(choices = ch, formula = formula, estimator = estimator), class = "spec_ticket")
}

run_spec <- function(spec) {
  if (missing(spec) || !inherits(spec, "spec_ticket"))
    stop("Pass the object that build_model() returned, e.g. run_spec(my_model).", call. = FALSE)
  now <- .check_choices()
  if (!identical(spec$choices, now))
    stop("The preregistration cell has changed since you built this model – rerun prereg() and build_model() so they agree.",
         call. = FALSE)
  ch  <- spec$choices
  hit <- .lookup(ch)
  ca  <- isTRUE(claim_align)
  .print_fit(ch, hit, "Your preregistered specification, read from the pre-computed grid:")
  if (ca && ch$my_outcome %in% .neg_framings)
    cat("  (negative framing – reverse-coded automatically: claim_align = TRUE)\n")
  if (ca && ch$my_predictor == "growth")
    cat("  (growth predictor – sign convention flipped automatically: claim_align = TRUE)\n")
  if (!ca)
    cat(sprintf("  (claim_align = FALSE: on this outcome's own scale b = %.5f, %s = %.3f; the class chart converts)\n",
                hit$estimate, if (ch$my_family == "beta") "z" else "t", hit$statistic))
  invisible(hit)
}

# One submission, used by both phases. The phase is prefixed to the free-text
# spec label, and all fourteen decisions travel inside that label; the form,
# its fields and the collection pipeline are frozen infrastructure.
.submit <- function(ch, hit, phase, lead) {
  fl <- .flip(ch)
  b <- fl * hit$estimate; tv <- fl * hit$statistic; r <- hit$r_ca
  spec_label <- paste0(phase, ": ", .spec_line(ch))

  FORM_ID <- "1FAIpQLSezoAEOnZUfP4pkfN28_XtEBwSyc2RLsXB-h8RPSegF7_t76A"
  field <- c(spec = "entry.832496914", b = "entry.1656311800", se = "entry.1337458262",
             t = "entry.1940779437", df = "entry.1682711955", n = "entry.1586392724",
             r = "entry.1660273001")
  value <- c(spec = spec_label, b = sprintf("%.5f", b),
             se = sprintf("%.5f", hit$std_error), t = sprintf("%.3f", tv),
             df = as.character(round(hit$df)), n = as.character(hit$n),
             r = sprintf("%.3f", r))
  query <- paste(vapply(names(field), function(k)
    paste0(field[[k]], "=", utils::URLencode(value[[k]], reserved = TRUE)),
    character(1)), collapse = "&")
  url <- sprintf("https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/%s/viewform?usp=pp_url&%s", FORM_ID, query)

  cat(lead, "\n\n")
  cat("  spec:", spec_label, "\n")
  cat(sprintf("  b = %.5f | se = %.5f | %s = %.3f | df = %d | n = %d | r = %.3f\n\n",
              b, hit$std_error, if (ch$my_family == "beta") "z" else "t", tv, round(hit$df), hit$n, r))
  cat("Open the link below (or copy the URL) – the form opens with every field\n")
  cat("pre-filled; just press Send.\n\n")
  cat(url, "\n")
  if (requireNamespace("htmltools", quietly = TRUE))
    print(htmltools::tags$p(htmltools::tags$a(href = url, target = "_blank",
                                              "Open the pre-filled form in a new tab")))
  invisible(list(spec = spec_label, b = b, se = hit$std_error, statistic = tv,
                 df = hit$df, n = hit$n, r = r, url = url))
}

report_result <- function() {
  ch  <- .check_choices()
  hit <- .lookup(ch)
  .submit(ch, hit, "declared",
          "Your declared submission (claim-aligned, straight from your preregistration):")
}
```
:::


Five analysts reanalysed a claim from the EU-frames case [@Teney2016DoesEUEconomic] for the Multi100 project [@AczelEtAl2026InvestigatingAnalyticalRobustness]; you are analyst no. 6. Read the full task description, the claim, and the five-analyst table of findings on the [Exercise overview](index.qmd) page (the [workshop slides](../slides/index.qmd) discuss the broader context of the project).

This page is the whole exercise, runnable in the browser: five tasks that take you from a setup check to two dots on the live class chart – one explored, one declared.



## Task 1 – Get yourself running {#task-1-setup}

Nothing conceptual here: the job is to reach the point where a line of R runs and the data are in front of you. Press **Run Code** on the cell below. If it prints the three lines it should, you are set up and everything else on this page will work.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}

## Answers – and the two traps

1.  **reproducibility** – rerunning the same code on the same data. Here it *failed* to match, but the activity is still reproducibility, and 'not reproduced' is the verdict.
2.  arguably still **reproducibility**, in a grey area – re-implementing on the same data in different software is technically a re-computation – but centring the predictor nudges towards **robustness**. Two packages can also implement the same estimator differently, so make sure you know what the function you call is doing.
3.  **replicability** – same question, independent new data chosen to be theoretically equivalent.
4.  **generalisability** – the impostor: new data *and* a new method at once. It is the fourth cell of the matrix, not one of the three we test today.

## Task 2, continued – name the estimand, draw the graph {#task-4-estimand-and-dag}

Before fitting anything, say what you are trying to estimate, in words. A template you can adapt:

> The **unit-specific quantity** is the change in mean cosmopolitan EU framing within a country-year associated with a one-point change in that country's unemployment rate. The **target population** is EU member states over 2004–2013. The **aggregation** is the average of those unit-specific effects, holding fixed each country's time-invariant traits and each year's EU-wide shocks.

That last clause is a causal claim, and a directed acyclic graph makes it checkable. A DAG is a picture of what causes what: variables are nodes, arrows run from cause to effect, and the rules of the graph then tell you which variables have to be adjusted for if the arrow you care about is to be read cleanly. Here is the graph that this exercise commits to.


::: {.cell layout-align="center"}
::: {.cell-output-display}
![The committed graph: unemployment to framing, with country and year as confounder pairs. The three pale nodes carry no arrows yet.](browser-lab_files/figure-html/dag-reference-1.png){fig-align='center' width=768}
:::
:::


Five arrows are drawn. `unemployment -> framing` is the path of interest. Above it, `country` is a common cause of both: stable national traits such as size, EU tenure and labour-market institutions move local unemployment and shape how people frame the EU. `year` does the same job for the EU-wide shocks that hit every country in the same calendar year. The three pale nodes below carry no arrows yet, because whether they belong is a decision you make rather than one that the exercise makes for you.

You build the graph yourself in the cells below, in ordinary R. `dagify()` takes one formula per arrow, written the way you write a model, so `framing ~ unemployment` is the arrow that runs *into* `framing`. Read the tilde as 'is caused by' rather than 'is regressed on' and the direction comes out right every time. Because each arrow is a line of R rather than a fragment of a string, an arrow you are unsure about can sit there commented out, and adopting it means deleting a `#`.

`dagify()` and `adjustmentSets()` are ready in this page already, so you can go straight to the next cell. The optional cell below adds the *picture*: it installs `ggdag`, which brings `igraph`, `ggraph` and four further dependencies with it – roughly 23 MB of download, and a noticeable pause on a slow connection. Run it if you want the plot. Skip it and everything else in Task 2 still works, because the figure above is the same graph.


::: {.cell autorun='true'}
```{webr}
#| include: false
#| autorun: true
# Graph machinery for Task 2. The adjustment-set question is answered here in
# base R rather than by dagitty, because dagitty reaches its graph algorithms
# through a JavaScript engine that a browser only exposes to a page served with
# cross-origin isolation headers (COOP and COEP). Without them the call fails
# with a JavaScript type error rather than an R error, so the browser lab
# cannot depend on it. These functions agree with `dagitty::adjustmentSets()`
# on every arrow combination that this task offers and on 378 random test graphs.

.dag_has_edge <- function(dag, a, b) any(dag$edges$from == a & dag$edges$to == b)

# A node counts as one of its own descendants, which is what the collider rule
# below needs.
.dag_descendants <- function(dag, v) {
  seen <- v
  frontier <- v
  while (length(frontier)) {
    kids <- setdiff(dag$edges$to[dag$edges$from %in% frontier], seen)
    seen <- c(seen, kids)
    frontier <- kids
  }
  seen
}

# Every simple path between two nodes, ignoring arrow direction. The recursion
# is safe only because a teaching graph is tiny.
.dag_paths <- function(dag, from, to) {
  out <- list()
  neighbours <- function(v) unique(c(dag$edges$to[dag$edges$from == v],
                                     dag$edges$from[dag$edges$to == v]))
  walk <- function(path) {
    v <- path[length(path)]
    if (v == to) {
      out[[length(out) + 1L]] <<- path
      return(invisible(NULL))
    }
    for (w in setdiff(neighbours(v), path)) walk(c(path, w))
  }
  walk(from)
  out
}

# A path is blocked by the set z if any node along it is either a non-collider
# inside z, or a collider with no descendant in z.
.dag_path_blocked <- function(dag, path, z) {
  if (length(path) < 3L) return(FALSE)
  for (i in seq(2L, length(path) - 1L)) {
    node <- path[i]
    collider <- .dag_has_edge(dag, path[i - 1L], node) &&
                .dag_has_edge(dag, path[i + 1L], node)
    if (collider) {
      if (!any(.dag_descendants(dag, node) %in% z)) return(TRUE)
    } else if (node %in% z) {
      return(TRUE)
    }
  }
  FALSE
}

.dagify_builtin <- function(..., exposure = NULL, outcome = NULL,
                            coords = NULL) {
  parts <- lapply(list(...), function(f) {
    child <- all.vars(f[[2]])
    parent <- all.vars(f[[3]])
    data.frame(from = parent, to = rep(child, length(parent)))
  })
  e <- do.call(rbind, parts)
  structure(list(edges = e, exposure = exposure, outcome = outcome,
                 nodes = unique(c(e$from, e$to))),
            class = "simple_dag")
}

# The backdoor criterion, brute-forced over subsets of the eligible variables:
# smallest sets first, and a set is skipped once it contains a set already
# found, which leaves only the minimal ones.
.adjustment_sets_builtin <- function(x, exposure = x$exposure,
                                     outcome = x$outcome, ...) {
  backdoor <- Filter(function(p) .dag_has_edge(x, p[2L], exposure),
                     .dag_paths(x, exposure, outcome))
  candidates <- setdiff(x$nodes, c(outcome, .dag_descendants(x, exposure)))
  found <- list()
  for (k in seq(0L, length(candidates))) {
    subsets <- if (k == 0L) list(character(0)) else
      utils::combn(candidates, k, simplify = FALSE)
    for (z in subsets) {
      if (any(vapply(found, function(f) all(f %in% z), logical(1)))) next
      if (all(vapply(backdoor, function(p) .dag_path_blocked(x, p, z),
                     logical(1)))) {
        found[[length(found) + 1L]] <- sort(z)
      }
    }
  }
  structure(found, class = "simple_dag_sets")
}

print.simple_dag_sets <- function(x, ...) {
  if (!length(x)) {
    cat("(no set of these variables closes every backdoor path)\n")
  } else {
    for (z in x) {
      cat(if (length(z)) paste0("{ ", paste(z, collapse = ", "), " }") else "{}",
          "\n", sep = "")
    }
  }
  invisible(x)
}

# Registered rather than left in the session: these cells do not evaluate in
# the global environment, so plain S3 dispatch would not find the method.
registerS3method("print", "simple_dag_sets", print.simple_dag_sets)

dagify <- .dagify_builtin
adjustmentSets <- .adjustment_sets_builtin
dag_engine <- "built-in"

# Whether dagitty could work here at all. Its JavaScript bridge needs
# SharedArrayBuffer, which a browser grants only to a cross-origin-isolated
# page, and the failure is a JavaScript error that tryCatch() cannot catch – so
# the question has to be asked before anything calls dagitty.
.dagitty_possible <- function() {
  isTRUE(tryCatch(
    as.numeric(webr::eval_js(
      "typeof SharedArrayBuffer === 'undefined' ? 0 : 1")) == 1,
    error = function(e) FALSE))
}
```
:::

Now specify the graph. The five committed arrows are live; the arguable ones are commented out, one substantive claim per line. Uncomment any you believe, then run the cell.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
my_dag <- dagify(
  # The path of interest, and the two confounder pairs that two-way fixed
  # effects soak up.
  framing      ~ unemployment,
  framing      ~ country,
  unemployment ~ country,
  framing      ~ year,
  unemployment ~ year,

  # GROWTH as a time-varying confounder: a slump raises unemployment and may
  # sour EU sentiment in the same year.
  # framing      ~ growth,
  # unemployment ~ growth,

  # BAILOUT as a mediator: unemployment triggers a financial-assistance
  # programme, which then shapes framing.
  # bailout ~ unemployment,
  # framing ~ bailout,

  # POLITICISATION of the EU by parties and elites as another cause of
  # framing. Multi100 instructed analysts to disregard it.
  # framing ~ politicisation,

  exposure = "unemployment",
  outcome  = "framing",
  # Coordinates for all seven nodes; the three not currently wired up are
  # simply ignored, so this block never needs editing.
  coords = list(
    x = c(unemployment = 0, framing = 3, country = 1, year = 2,
          growth = 0.9, bailout = 1.5, politicisation = 3),
    y = c(unemployment = 0, framing = 0, country = 1.4, year = 1.4,
          growth = -1.0, bailout = -1.2, politicisation = -0.95)))

adjustmentSets(my_dag)
```
:::


With the five committed arrows the minimal adjustment set is `{ country, year }` – exactly what a two-way fixed-effects model absorbs. Country fixed effects adjust for `country` and year fixed effects adjust for `year`, so the model you will fit in Task 3 and the graph you just wrote are one identification claim in two languages.

Now uncomment the growth pair and run the cell again. The set becomes `{ country, growth, year }`, because a slump varies within a country over time and fixed effects only remove country-constant and year-common variation. Nothing in the Task 3 model reaches it, and your specification would need `growth` as a co-predictor to match your beliefs – a choice waiting for you on the menu in Task 5. The bailout arrows behave differently. A mediator sits on the path you are trying to measure, so the adjustment set does not grow when you add one; adjusting for it would strip out part of the very effect you are after.

## Why 'exploratory'?

Because you chose this specification after seeing what several specifications do, it cannot carry the guarantee that a declared choice carries – no one can rule out that it might have been chosen *because* of its result. This is something we almost never know in the case of published papers, unless their analysis has been pre-registered and departures from the pre-registration documented. In this course exploration is a natural step, but you'll also practise pre-registering your chosen analysis; you will submit twice: once here, and once in Task 5.

The point of preregistration is that you commit to a choice **before** you see what it does. It stops you quietly picking the specification that happens to give the answer you wanted. ## Hint – from menu speak to model syntax

The formula uses the column names of `euframes`: the outcome you preregistered on the left of `~`, the predictor terms on the right. For the baseline declaration it is `mcosmo ~ unemp`; with the log form it would be `mcosmo ~ log(unemp)`; with a co-predictor, `mcosmo ~ unemp + growth`. The estimator is the menu code itself, in quotes: `"fe_twoway"`, `"fe_country"`, `"re"` or `"pooled_cl"`. You do not write the fixed-effects or clustering syntax here – the estimator code stands for it, and Task 3 showed what it expands to. The Level 2 and Level 3 choices never appear in the formula at all: they select which version of the panel the result was computed on and which fitting convention was used.
:::
